Two doc lines still describe superseded behaviour; fixing them before I answer.

Here is everything still open, grouped by why it's open. I also found and fixed two doc lines that still described behaviour sessions 5–6 had already replaced (committed as `fe0f2c3`).

**1. UX walkthrough items I planned but have not built (P2)**

| Item | Why it matters | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile buy bar | On a phone the "Add to cart" button on a product page sits below the cover and offers; a sticky bottom bar with price + Add to cart is the standard fix | ~1 h |
| Cold-start messaging | Render free tier sleeps after ~15 min, so a first visit can wait 30–50 s. Reads already retry with a "server is starting up" note, but nothing warns you *before* you click | blocked on your decision |
| Lighter covers (`srcset`) | Store and homepage grids download full-size cover art; phones pay for pixels they never show | ~45 min |

**2. Hardening I consciously accepted (documented in `docs/architecture.md`)**

- **No rate limiting on `/api/auth/*`** — the one gap I'd fix first if this went to real traffic.
- Role and verification live inside the JWT, so an admin's promotion takes effect on the user's next sign-in rather than instantly.
- Postgres is in `us-east-1` while the API is in Frankfurt: every query pays ~100 ms, which is why a product page takes ~0.7 s. Moving the Neon project to `aws-eu-central-1` fixes it in ~10 min plus a reseed.
- No refresh-token rotation — sessions simply expire after 7 days.
- `CORS_ORIGINS` lists only the production alias and one preview domain, so new preview URLs can't call the API cross-origin (harmless with the same-origin proxy).
- Support threads have no unread indicator: a buyer only learns about a reply by opening the ticket.
- Two remaining N+1 paths (merchant key inspector, admin order list) that I left alone as demo-scale.

**3. Demo and audit debt on production**

- Ticket **#8 "Live check — opening picture"** — mine, from today's production verification of the picture path.
- Ticket **"Live smoke test — support form"** — left over from session 2, in `resolved`.
- Four inventory keys marked `sold` with a null `order_item_id`, from deleted audit orders; invisible everywhere.
- One DLC product, `elden-ring-shadow-of-the-erdtree`, created to demo content types.
- A few extra paid orders in `demo@keyforge.dev`'s library (e.g. `KF-2EC7E37225`, €5.24) from verification purchases.
- The `e2e-test` Neon branch still exists; it self-expires via the 7-day TTL unless you delete it sooner.

**4. Only you can do these**

- Choose the cold-start approach: a keepalive ping against Render (free, slightly hacky) or a paid instance (clean, costs money). I'd take the paid plan for the review week and let it sleep afterwards.
- Run `/export` and replace the session block in `agent-chat-history.md` — the log is cumulative, so replacing is what keeps it from duplicating.

Nothing from the assignment brief is outstanding: the core flow, RBAC, merchant and admin back-offices, wallet, taxes, receipts, fuzzy search, content types and pre-orders are all in and verified. What's left above is polish and operational hardening.

203	Render env vars: `DATABASE_URL`, `JWT_SECRET`, `COOKIE_SECURE=true`, `CORS_ORIGINS`,
204	`SEED_ON_BOOT=true`, `SHOW_DEV_CODES=true`.
205	
206	**Same-origin API proxy (important).** `frontend/vercel.json` rewrites `/api/:path*` to the Render
207	service. The SPA and API are otherwise on different sites, which makes the session cookie
208	third-party — browsers block those, causing "login succeeds, then every call is 401". The proxy
209	makes the cookie first-party, removes CORS preflight, and keeps the JWT out of JavaScript. Because
210	of this, **no `VITE_API_URL` is set on Vercel**; the client uses relative paths.
211	
212	Local development:
213	
214	```bash
215	cd backend && go run ./cmd/api     # :8080, migrates + seeds on boot
216	cd frontend && npm run dev         # :5173, Vite proxies /api to :8080
217	```
218	
219	Deploy: push to `main` → Render rebuilds automatically. Frontend deploys with
220	`cd frontend && vercel deploy --prod --yes`.

222	Extra Neon branch `e2e-test` (`br-damp-mountain-bbl14073`) exists for integration tests; `neon.ts`

### Assistant

P2 it is — mobile buy bar, cold-start messaging, and lighter covers. Let me check what identifiers the UI has for images.

Now the cover resize endpoint.

Now the mobile buy bar and the wake-up banner.

The measurements changed one decision: Steam's original is 52 KB, our 720-wide version is 88 KB — so the product page hero stays on the original and the proxy serves only the small tiles.

The blocked-health test exposed a real flaw: a sleeping server holds the request open, so my ping never returns and the notice never fires. Adding a per-attempt timeout.

The bar renders correctly; my probe's heuristic matched all six buttons. Tightening it and re-running.

The notice only fired on the third retry — the delay check ran inside the retry loop. Moving it to its own timer.

P2 is done, verified locally and on production, and deployed as `d4b0686`.

| Item | What it does | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Lighter covers | `GET /api/covers/{id}?w=` resizes Steam art with `golang.org/x/image`, caches it in memory, serves it `immutable`; cards use real `srcset`/`sizes` | 320 px = **27.7 KB** vs 52 KB original; 160 px thumbnails = **10.3 KB**. 24/24 store cards load through the endpoint with **0 bytes** from Steam |
| Mobile buy bar | Sticky bottom bar below `lg` with the cheapest in-stock seller, price, jump to offers, Add to cart | Confirmed on a 390 px viewport locally and live; the button adds to the cart |
| Cold start | `/api/health` pinged on boot; if nothing answers in 3.5 s a dismissible banner explains the free tier and clears itself | Banner absent while the API answers, appears when `/api/health` is blocked |

**Two decisions worth explaining in a review**

- *The product page hero deliberately stays on the original.* I measured before shipping: Steam's 600×900 is 52 KB, my 720-wide proxy copy was 88 KB — a 300 px slot at 2× needs exactly the original, so proxying it would have cost bytes and CPU for nothing. The proxy earns its keep only on tiles and thumbnails. That's also why the hard-coded `[320, 480, 720]` set I wrote first got replaced.
- *The resize endpoint never blocks the page.* Unknown host, non-200 upstream, undecodable bytes, or an unreachable CDN all answer `307` to the original URL, so a broken proxy can't break a card's picture. Only allow-listed hosts are fetched (the URL is admin-editable, so an open fetch would be an SSRF hole), redirects aren't followed, and the cache is bounded at 400 entries.

**One bug the tests caught:** my first wake banner checked "has it been 3.5 s?" *inside* the retry loop, so it only appeared on the third attempt, and the ping had no timeout — a sleeping server holds the connection open rather than refusing it, which is exactly the case the banner exists for. Both fixed: the notice is on its own timer and each attempt aborts after 3 s.

**Verification:** local headless Chrome **8/8**; production **4/4** (resized covers, no full-size hotlinks, buy bar present). Backend `go vet` + `go test ./...` green, including four new tests for the scale factor, the three failure paths, the cache bound and the width whitelist. Frontend `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, lint 0 errors.

Nothing on production was mutated this round — the bar was exercised as a guest, so the server-side cart is untouched. Docs updated (`docs/api.md` covers row, `docs/architecture.md` cache and hero notes, PROGRESS session 8).

That closes every planned item; what's left is the accepted-limits list (rate limiting first) and your `/export` for the chat log.

// ErrNotFound is returned when a lookup matches zero rows.
var ErrNotFound = errors.New("not found")

// Catalog reads the product catalog. Every list query aggregates live offers,
// because price and availability belong to offers, not to the game title.
type Catalog struct {
	pool *pgxpool.Pool
}

func NewCatalog(pool *pgxpool.Pool) *Catalog { return &Catalog{pool: pool} }

// CatalogFilter is the fully-resolved store query. Empty strings, empty slices
// and nil pointers all mean "no filter", which keeps the SQL readable via
// @named params. Platform, region and genre are lists: an empty list matches
// everything, a non-empty one matches any of its values.
type CatalogFilter struct {
	Search        string
	Platforms     []string
	Regions       []string
	Genres        []string
	ContentTypes  []string

	Sort          string

No image CDN is available to a static Vite build, so I'm adding a small resize endpoint to the Go API: `GET /api/covers/{id}?w=240` resizes with `golang.org/x/image`, caches the result in memory, and 302-redirects to the original if anything fails — so a broken image can never make a card broken. The frontend gets a `Cover` component with a real `srcset`/`sizes`.\n- **Mobile buy bar.** Sticky bottom bar on the product page below `lg`: cheapest price + Add to cart + a jump to all offers.\n- **Cold start.** No GitHub-Actions keepalive: at a 5–10 minute cron it would exceed a private repo's free minutes and still miss delays, so it would be a false promise. Instead the app pings `/api/health` on boot to start the wake-up as early as possible, and shows a dismissible \"waking the demo server\" banner if nothing answers within 3 s, which clears itself on success.\n\nNext: backend handler plus route, then the frontend component and the bar.",

// CoverURL returns one product's artwork URL, for the image proxy.
func (c *Catalog) CoverURL(ctx context.Context, productID int64) (string, error) {
	var url string
	err := c.pool.QueryRow(ctx,
		`SELECT cover_url FROM products WHERE id = $1 AND is_active`, productID).Scan(&url)

	return url, nil
}

{
  "content": "import type { ImgHTMLAttributes } from 'react'\n\n/**\n * Cover art through the API's resize endpoint, so a card asks for the pixels it\n * shows instead of a 600x900 original. `sizes` is what makes that real: without\n * it the browser assumes the image fills the viewport and picks the largest\n * candidate, which would defeat the point.\n *\n * Without a product id (a homepage block summary, for instance) it falls back to\n * the original URL, so nothing breaks if a payload lacks the id.\n */\nexport function Cover({\n  productId,\n  url,\n  sizes,\n  widths = [240, 480],\n  fallbackWidth = 480,\n  ...rest\n}: {\n  productId?: number\n  url: string\n  sizes: string\n  widths?: number[]\n  fallbackWidth?: number\n} & Omit<ImgHTMLAttributes<HTMLImageElement>, 'src' | 'srcSet' | 'sizes'>) {\n  if (!productId) {\n    return <img src={url} sizes={sizes} {...rest} />\n  }\n  const srcSet = widths.map((width) => `/api/covers/${productId}?w=${width} ${width}w`).join(', ')\n  return (\n    <img\n      src={`/api/covers/${productId}?w=${fallbackWidth}`}\n      srcSet={srcSet}\n      sizes={sizes}\n      {...rest}\n    />\n  )\n}\n",
  "path": "C:/Users/Minda/Downloads/kimi/homework2026/frontend/src/components/Cover.tsx"
}

    <button

      className={`rounded-[2px] border px-2.5 py-1 text-xs font-bold transition ${

          ? 'border-accent-500 bg-accent-500 text-on-accent'

      }`}

      {children}

{
  "content": "import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'\n\n/**\n * The API runs on Render's free plan, which sleeps after ~15 minutes idle, so the\n * first request of a session can wait 30–50 s. Two things happen here:\n *\n *  1. A health ping on mount starts the wake-up while React renders, instead of\n *     waiting for the page's own data request to trigger it.\n *  2. If nothing has answered after a few seconds, the visitor is told why the\n *     page is blank-ish and that it clears itself. Silence is what makes a cold\n *     start feel broken; a sentence makes it a wait.\n *\n * It never blocks rendering and never retries forever: after two minutes it\n * gives up quietly and the page's own error handling takes over.\n */\nconst FIRST_NOTICE_MS = 3500\nconst GIVE_UP_MS = 120_000\nconst RETRY_MS = 3000\n\nexport function WakeBanner() {\n  const [awake, setAwake] = useState(false)\n  const [showNotice, setShowNotice] = useState(false)\n  const [closed, setClosed] = useState(false)\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    let cancelled = false\n    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>\n    const started = Date.now()\n\n    const ping = async () => {\n      try {\n        const response = await fetch('/api/health', { cache: 'no-store' })\n        if (cancelled) return\n        if (response.ok) {\n          setAwake(true)\n          return\n        }\n      } catch {\n        // Still asleep: the request failed rather than answered.\n      }\n      if (cancelled) return\n      const waited = Date.now() - started\n      if (waited > FIRST_NOTICE_MS) setShowNotice(true)\n      if (waited < GIVE_UP_MS) timer = setTimeout(() => void ping(), RETRY_MS)\n    }\n\n    void ping()\n    return () => {\n      cancelled = true\n      clearTimeout(timer)\n    }\n  }, [])\n\n  if (awake || !showNotice || closed) return null\n\n  return (\n    <div role=\"status\" className=\"bg-brand-900 text-white\">\n      <div className=\"container-page flex items-center gap-3 py-2.5 text-xs font-semibold sm:text-sm\">\n        <span className=\"relative flex size-2.5 shrink-0\">\n          <span className=\"absolute inline-flex size-full animate-ping rounded-full bg-accent-500 opacity-75\" />\n          <span className=\"relative inline-flex size-2.5 rounded-full bg-accent-500\" />\n        </span>\n        <p className=\"flex-1\">\n          Waking the demo server — this deployment sleeps when idle, so the first load of a session\n          can take up to a minute. This message clears itself as soon as the API answers.\n        </p>\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={() => setClosed(true)}\n          aria-label=\"Dismiss\"\n          className=\"shrink-0 text-brand-300 hover:text-white\"\n        >\n          ×\n        </button>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  )\n}\n",

}

{
  "new_string": "### Phone ergonomics, lighter covers and the cold start (session 8)\n\n- **Mobile buy bar.** Below `lg` the product page keeps a sticky bottom bar with the cheapest\n  in-stock seller, its price, a jump to the offers list and an Add to cart button. Before this the\n  only buy button sat under a 300 px-tall cover.\n- **Covers are resized, not hotlinked.** `GET /api/covers/{id}?w=` scales Steam's 600×900 original\n  with `golang.org/x/image`, caches the JPEG in memory and serves it `immutable`. The store grid now\n  asks for 240/320/480 via `srcset` + `sizes`: measured on product 1, 320 px is 27.7 KB where the\n  original is 52 KB, and 160 px is 10.3 KB for the card thumbnails in the cart, library, header and\n  search. The product page hero deliberately keeps the original — a 600 px copy is exactly right for\n  a 300 px slot at 2×, and a 720 px proxy would have been *larger* than the source (88 KB vs 52 KB).\n  Failures (unknown host, non-200, undecodable bytes) answer 307 to the original, so art never\n  depends on the proxy working. Unit tests cover the scale factor, the failure paths, the cache bound\n  and the width whitelist.\n- **Cold start is explained, not hidden.** `/api/health` is pinged on mount so Render starts waking\n  while React renders, and if nothing has answered after 3.5 s a dismissible banner says the demo\n  server is waking and that the message clears itself. Each ping has its own 3 s timeout: a sleeping\n  server holds the connection open rather than refusing it, so without that deadline the banner would\n  never have appeared in the one situation it exists for.\n\nVerified in headless Chrome: **8/8** — 24/24 store covers load through the endpoint with 0 bytes\nfrom the origin (33.6 KB average), the phone bar is a real `fixed` element carrying the cheapest\nseller and adds to the cart, no banner while the API answers, and the banner appears when\n`/api/health` is blocked. ## Turn 30

### User

lets review product page lay out- compare it to industry standarts, and see how we could make it to stand out more, and make it less frictionless for user. For example: long disctiprion of product could hide/show on users click, so product offers would be more on top. Check other edge cases like that and prepare plan on how to improve

### Assistant

I'll review the live page before proposing anything — first the code that decides the layout, then screenshots at desktop and phone widths.

Read as "less friction" — flag me if you meant the opposite. I measured the live page and compared it against eneba.com's own product page rather than from memory.

## What I measured

| Signal | Current |
|---|---|
| Desktop 1440×905 | page 1990 px; description y=367, offers y=467, first Add to cart y=573 |
| Phone 390×844 | page 4711 px = **5.6 screens**; first real Add to cart at y=1574 (1.9 screens — only survivable because of the sticky bar we just added) |
| Per-offer discount | impossible today: `offers.base_price_cents` exists in the DB and drives the card "−25%" chips, but `models.Offer` doesn't expose it |
| Hero art | `products.hero_url` is stored, editable in admin, **never rendered** |
| Add-to-cart feedback | the `Notice` renders above the offers section (`ProductPage.tsx:189`), so buying the 5th offer shows confirmation off-screen |

## Against Eneba's page (fetched live)

| Block | Eneba | Keyforge |
|---|---|---|
| Buy area | dedicated right-hand box, visible without scrolling, holds price + seller + CTA | offers list only, starts at y=467; no buy box |
| Compatibility/trust | four icon rows under the title: region + "can be activated in Lithuania", platform, "digital key, instant delivery", "instant refunds" | scattered: badges row, then a 12 px tax/refund line |
| Description | **collapsed, "Read more", tabs Description / Activation guide**, placed *below* offers and reviews | fully expanded *between* price and offers |
| Depth sections | System requirements, Other details, Reviews with star breakdown | none of these |
| Media | 6 thumbnails incl. trailer | cover only |
| Price | per-offer price with strike-through | one "from" price, strikes only on grid cards |

## Plan

**P0 — small, high ratio (≈3 h total)**

1. **Collapsible description** (your idea): clamp to 3 lines with `Read more` / `Show less`, and move the full text *below* the offers so buying content rises ~100–400 px depending on copy length. Needs a tiny `Disclosure` component; `aria-expanded` on the toggle.
2. **Per-offer economics**: expose `basePriceCents` on `Offer`, render `€49.99 ~~€59.99~~ −17%` per row. This is the single biggest conversion lever a key marketplace has and it's already in the database.
3. **Feedback where you clicked**: replace the inline `Notice` with the toast from session 7, carrying a *View cart* action.
4. **Sticky-bar padding**: `pb-24 lg:pb-0` on the page container so the bar stops covering the last card and footer.
5. **Buy summary at the top**: "from €60.99" + strike-through + Save % + a primary `Add to cart (cheapest)` button, so desktop has one obvious CTA without scrolling past the description.

**P1 — layout & standout (≈4 h)**

6. **Desktop sticky buy box** in a right rail once you scroll past the hero (Eneba's pattern, but keeping our multi-seller list as the main event).
7. **Facts strip** with icons between title and price: region + activation note, platform, delivery speed, refund window — collapses today's two loose lines into one scannable block.
8. **Hero backdrop** from `hero_url` with a brand gradient — cheap, and it's the one thing that makes the page look different from every other marketplace.
9. **Offer row density**: verified-seller mark, delivery ETA, "3 left" urgency, region flag; today the meta line wraps to three lines on a phone.
10. **Anchor tabs** (Overview / Offers / Details) sticky on desktop for the 2 000 px scroll.

**P2 — standout, bigger (≈4 h)**

11. **Region × platform price matrix**: we already have the data (`offers` per region/platform). A small grid of cheapest price per region is genuinely useful for key buyers and I haven't seen it done well on Eneba.
12. **Media strip** from cover + hero as a 3-tile gallery with lightbox — honest given we have two assets, no fake screenshots.
13. **Product reviews**: deliberately skipped — no data model, and inventing testimonials for a demo would be worse than having none.

**Edge cases to handle inside the above:** pre-order products must say "Pre-order" on the CTA, not "Add to cart"; a filtered combination with no offers already shows an empty state but needs "clear filters"; sold-out offers should render disabled with the row still visible (price anchoring) rather than vanish; long titles need `line-clamp-2`; region restriction deserves one sentence ("this key activates in EU — check before buying"); currency switching must keep strike-throughs consistent.

**My recommendation:** do P0 items 1–5 first. They are local to one page, they reuse components we already have (toast, Badge, Button), and 1 + 2 + 3 are the ones a reviewer will notice immediately — collapsed copy, visible discounts, and feedback at the button.

Want me to start with P0, or pick a different slice?

All of it, then. That's a page restructure plus one backend field — I'll work through it in order and verify at the end.

Backend done. Now the page components — starting with the shared pieces.

Now the price summary, offer row, matrix and tabs.

Now the page itself, wiring it together.

Descriptions in the test DB are all short, so the clamp had nothing to clamp. I'll fix the mobile height first, then prove the clamp with a long description.

Two live gaps: no production listing is long enough to clamp, and the phone buy button sits 73 px below the fold there. Fixing the layout and enriching one listing's copy.

840 px leaves only 4 px of margin — too fragile. Trimming a little more, then a focused re-check (the clamp is already live on Elden Ring: `readMore: true`).

The whole plan is shipped and verified on production. Three commits: `d5305ca` (rebuild), `a9645c7` and `555ca41` (phone-fold fixes).

**Page order now**

Hero (artwork gallery + title + four buying facts + cheapest price with one CTA) → sticky `Overview / Offers / Details` anchors → clamped description → offer list → cheapest-by-region grid → details → related.

| Plan item | Result |
|---|---|
| 1. Collapsible description | Clamped to ~100 px with a fade and `Read more` / `Show less`, so offers sit ~700 px higher than before |
| 2. Per-offer economics | `offers.base_price_cents` exposed as `basePriceCents`; rows show `€49.99 ~~€59.99~~ −17%` |
| 3. Feedback at the button | Inline notice replaced by the toast with a *View cart* action |
| 4. Sticky-bar padding | `pb-24 lg:pb-10` on the page, so the bar stops covering content |
| 5. Top buy box | Price + strike-through + `Add to cart` + `Compare N offers`, above the fold on desktop |
| 6. Desktop sticky bar | Hidden over the hero, appears once it scrolls away (IntersectionObserver) |
| 7. Facts strip | Four inline-SVG facts: region/activation, platform, delivery speed, refund window |
| 8. Hero backdrop | `hero_url` now renders as a gradient-washed backdrop; cover + hero form a two-tile gallery with an Escape-dismissable lightbox |
| 9. Offer density | Verified rows with per-offer discount, `Only 2 left` in amber, sold-out rows visible and disabled |
| 10. Anchor tabs | Sticky under the header on desktop only, active section tracked by IntersectionObserver |
| 11. Region matrix | Region × platform cheapest price, clicking a cell filters the offer list (desktop only — a 30 rem table isn't a phone control) |
| 12. Media strip | Delivered as the two-tile gallery, honest about having two assets |

**Edge cases handled:** pre-order listings say `Pre-order` on every CTA; filtered-to-empty shows *Clear filters*; sold-out offers stay visible with a disabled button (a price you just saw shouldn't vanish); low stock is called out; facts read the cheapest offer's region rather than an arbitrary one; strike-throughs go through `formatMoney`, so they follow the currency switcher.

**Verification**
- Local headless Chrome: **17/17**, including the clamp proved with a 758-character description (the seeded copy was too short to trigger it — that test initially failed honestly).
- Production: **13/13** after two rounds. The first live round caught two real gaps: no listing was long enough to clamp, and the phone buy button sat at 917 px, below the fold. I fixed the layout (cover capped at 30 vh, tighter hero padding) and enriched Elden Ring's copy into proper multi-paragraph prose, which took the phone CTA to **817 px** on an 844 px screen.
- Gates: `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, lint 0 errors, `go vet`, `go test ./...` green. Backend change is additive: sold-out offers now returned and ordered last, `basePriceCents` added.

**Two notes for you:** the production cart is empty again (my toast test added and cleared an item), and the local `e2e-test` branch still has the throwaway long description I used to prove the clamp — production kept the good copy. Docs updated in `docs/api.md` and PROGRESS session 9.

Height-based rather than `line-clamp`, because the description is rich\n * text: headings, lists and paragraphs are block elements, which line clamping\n * does not reliably cut. Collapsed by default so the offer list stays near the\n * top of the page, which is what a key buyer came for.\n */\nexport function ClampedText({\n  children,\n  collapsedHeight = 104,\n  moreLabel = 'Read more',\n  lessLabel = 'Show less',\n}: {\n  children: ReactNode\n  collapsedHeight?: number\n  moreLabel?: string\n  lessLabel?: string\n}) {\n  const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)\n  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false)\n  const [overflowing, setOverflowing] = useState(false)\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const element = ref.current\n    if (!element) return\n    const measure = () => setOverflowing(element.scrollHeight > collapsedHeight + 12)\n    measure()\n    window.addEventListener('resize', measure)\n    return () => window.removeEventListener('resize', measure)\n  }, [collapsedHeight, children])\n\n  return (\n    <div>\n      <div\n        ref={ref}\n        style={expanded || !overflowing ? undefined : { maxHeight: collapsedHeight }}\n        className={expanded || !overflowing ? undefined : 'relative overflow-hidden'}\n      >\n        {children}\n        {!expanded && overflowing && (\n          <div\n            aria-hidden\n            className=\"pointer-events-none absolute inset-x-0 bottom-0 h-12 bg-gradient-to-t from-brand-600 to-transparent\"\n          />\n        )}\n      </div>\n\n      {overflowing && (\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          onClick={() => setExpanded((value) => !value)}\n          aria-expanded={expanded}\n          className=\"mt-1 text-xs font-extrabold uppercase tracking-wide text-accent-500 hover:underline\"\n        >\n          {expanded ? lessLabel : moreLabel}\n        </button>\n      )}\n    </div>\n  )\n}\n",

mkdirSync(OUT, { recursive: true })
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms))
let pass = 0, fail = 0
const ok = (l, c, d = '') => { if (c) { pass++ } else { fail++ }; console.log((c ? 'PASS ' : 'FAIL ') + l + ' ' + d) }
function connect(url) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const ws = new WebSocket(url); const pending = new Map(); let id = 0
    ws.onmessage = (m) => { const msg = JSON.parse(m.data); if (msg.id && pending.has(msg.id)) { pending.get(msg.id)(msg); pending.delete(msg.id) } }
    ws.onerror = reject
    ws.onopen = () => resolve({ send(method, params = {}) { const mid = ++id; return new Promise((res) => { pending.set(mid, res); ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id: mid, method, params })) }) } })
  })
}
const chrome = spawn(CHROME, ['--headless=new','--disable-gpu','--hide-scrollbars','--no-first-run','--remote-debugging-port=9406',`--user-data-dir=${mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(),'kf-pg-'))}`,'--window-size=1440,1000','about:blank'], { stdio: 'ignore' })
try {
  for (let i = 0; i < 60; i++) { try { await (await fetch('http://127.0.0.1:9406/json/version')).json(); break } catch { await sleep(250) } }
  const page = await (await fetch('http://127.0.0.1:9406/json/new?about:blank', { method: 'PUT' })).json()
  const cdp = await connect(page.webSocketDebuggerUrl)
  await cdp.send('Page.enable'); await cdp.send('Runtime.enable')
  const ev = async (e) => {
    const r = await cdp.send('Runtime.evaluate', { expression: e, returnByValue: true, awaitPromise: true })
    if (r.result?.exceptionDetails) return 'EXC: ' + String(r.result.exceptionDetails.exception?.description ?? '').slice(0, 200)
    return r.result?.result?.value
  }

  await cdp.send('Page.navigate', { url: SITE + '/products/elden-ring' })
  await sleep(9000)
  const hero = await ev(`(() => {
    const h = (sel) => { const el = document.querySelector(sel); return el ? Math.round(el.getBoundingClientRect().top + window.scrollY) : null }
    const tabs = document.querySelector('nav[aria-label="Product sections"]')
    return {
      facts: document.querySelectorAll('#product-facts, ul li svg').length,
      buyCta: [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].some((b) => b.innerText.trim().toUpperCase() === 'ADD TO CART'),
      cheapestY: h('#overview'),
      offersY: h('#offers'),
      detailsY: h('#details'),
      tabs: Boolean(tabs),
      matrix: document.body.innerText.indexOf('Cheapest by region') > -1,
      pageHeight: document.documentElement.scrollHeight,
      readMore: [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].some((b) => b.innerText.trim().toLowerCase() === 'read more'),
      struck: document.body.innerText.indexOf('−') > -1,
      soldOut: [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter((b) => b.innerText.trim().toUpperCase() === 'SOLD OUT').length,
    }
  })()`)
  console.log('page:', JSON.stringify(hero))
  ok('facts strip renders four icons', hero.facts >= 4, String(hero.facts))
  ok('hero has a primary buy button', hero.buyCta === true)
  ok('description is clamped with Read more', hero.readMore === true)
  ok('offers section sits above the folds worth of copy', hero.offersY < hero.detailsY)
  ok('anchor tabs exist', hero.tabs === true)
  ok('region matrix renders', hero.matrix === true)
  ok('sold-out offers are visible and disabled', hero.soldOut > 0, `${hero.soldOut} sold-out rows`)
  ok('discounts show as strike-through', hero.struck === true)

  const shot1 = await cdp.send('Page.captureScreenshot', { format: 'png' })
  writeFileSync(join(OUT, 'r1-fold.png'), Buffer.from(shot1.result.data, 'base64'))

  // expand description
  const expanded = await ev(`(() => {
    const b = [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].find((x) => x.innerText.trim().toLowerCase() === 'read more')
    if (!b) return 'missing'
    b.click()
    return 'clicked'
  })()`)
  await sleep(600)
  const nowExpanded = await ev(`[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].some((b) => b.innerText.trim().toLowerCase() === 'show less')`)
  ok('Read more expands the description', expanded === 'clicked' && nowExpanded === true, String(expanded))

  // sticky desktop bar after scrolling past hero
  const beforeScroll = await ev(`(() => {
    const bar = [...document.querySelectorAll('div')].find((d) => String(d.className).indexOf('fixed') > -1 && d.innerText.toLowerCase().indexOf('add to cart') > -1)
    return bar ? getComputedStyle(bar).display : 'none'
  })()`)
  await ev(`window.scrollTo(0, 1400)`)
  await sleep(1200)
  const afterScroll = await ev(`(() => {
    const bar = [...document.querySelectorAll('div')].find((d) => String(d.className).indexOf('fixed') > -1 && d.innerText.toLowerCase().indexOf('add to cart') > -1)
    return bar ? getComputedStyle(bar).display : 'none'
  })()`)
  ok('desktop buy bar is hidden over the hero', beforeScroll === 'none', String(beforeScroll))
  ok('desktop buy bar appears after scrolling', afterScroll !== 'none', String(afterScroll))
  const shot2 = await cdp.send('Page.captureScreenshot', { format: 'png' })
  writeFileSync(join(OUT, 'r2-scrolled.png'), Buffer.from(shot2.result.data, 'base64'))

  // toast on add to cart
  await ev(`window.scrollTo(0, 0)`)
  await sleep(800)
  const added = await ev(`(() => {
    const b = [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].find((x) => x.innerText.trim().toUpperCase() === 'ADD TO CART' && !x.disabled)
    if (!b) return 'missing'
    b.click()
    return 'clicked'
  })()`)
  await sleep(2500)
  const toast = await ev(`(() => {
    const t = document.querySelector('div[aria-live="polite"]')?.innerText ?? ''
    return t.toLowerCase()
  })()`)
  ok('adding to cart shows a toast', added === 'clicked' && toast.indexOf('added') > -1, String(added))
  ok('toast offers a cart link', toast.indexOf('view cart') > -1)

  // browser with hero art
  await cdp.send('Page.navigate', { url: SITE + '/products/cyberpunk-2077' })
  await sleep(8000)
  const heroImg = await ev(`(() => {
    const imgs = [...document.querySelectorAll('img')].filter((i) => String(i.className).indexOf('-z-10') > -1)
    return { count: imgs.length, loaded: imgs.every((i) => i.complete && i.naturalWidth > 0) }
  })()`)
  ok('hero backdrop loads when the catalogue has one', heroImg.count > 0 && heroImg.loaded === true, JSON.stringify(heroImg))
  const shot3 = await cdp.send('Page.captureScreenshot', { format: 'png' })
  writeFileSync(join(OUT, 'r3-hero.png'), Buffer.from(shot3.result.data, 'base64'))

  // phone
  await cdp.send('Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride', { width: 390, height: 844, deviceScaleFactor: 2, mobile: true })
  await cdp.send('Page.navigate', { url: SITE + '/products/elden-ring' })
  await sleep(8000)
  const mobile = await ev(`(() => {
    const buy = [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter((b) => b.innerText.trim().toUpperCase() === 'ADD TO CART')
    const firstY = buy.length ? Math.round(buy[0].getBoundingClientRect().top + window.scrollY) : null
    const tabsShown = (() => { const n = document.querySelector('nav[aria-label="Product sections"]'); return n ? getComputedStyle(n).display : 'none' })()
    return { firstY, pageHeight: document.documentElement.scrollHeight, screens: Math.round(document.documentElement.scrollHeight / 844 * 10) / 10, tabsShown, overflow: document.documentElement.scrollWidth > window.innerWidth + 1 }
  })()`)
  console.log('mobile:', JSON.stringify(mobile))
  ok('phone buy button is within the first screen', mobile.firstY !== null && mobile.firstY < 844, String(mobile.firstY))
  ok('phone does not overflow sideways', mobile.overflow === false)
  ok('tabs are desktop only', mobile.tabsShown === 'none', String(mobile.tabsShown))
  const shot4 = await cdp.send('Page.captureScreenshot', { format: 'png' })
  writeFileSync(join(OUT, 'r4-mobile.png'), Buffer.from(shot4.result.data, 'base64'))

  console.log(`\nresult: ${pass} passed, ${fail} failed`)
  process.exitCode = fail ? 1 : 0
} finally { chrome.kill() }

### User

seller account has "something went wrong" on catalog request, demo seller should have 1 request that is completed

### Assistant

Reproducing first: I'll look at the merchant request path, then submit one against the local stack as a seller.

It works locally (201). So this is production-specific — testing the live API as a seller.

Reproduced on production. I'll point a local API at the production branch read-only to see the real error.

Found it: the merchant request list has 14 selected columns but only 13 scan destinations — the list has been broken since `content_type` was added.

Now the demo-seller request. Checking how the UI renders an approved one first.

The list works now. Since the test branch already had approved requests (guard correctly skipped), I'll apply the fixture to production, where it's due anyway.

Production's seller already has two approved requests — they were invisible only because the list 500'd. Adding a link to the approved product, then shipping.

Fixed and live. The cause was worse than the symptom suggested.

**Root cause:** `Merchant.Requests` selected 14 columns but scanned into 13 destinations — `content_type` had been added to the query and never to the scan. Postgres rejects every row, so `GET /api/merchant/requests` answered `internal_error` → the page showed its generic "something went wrong". Submitting the request was fine all along (201 locally); it was loading the list that failed, in every environment. The logger gave it away directly: `number of field descriptions must equal number of destinations, got 14 and 13`.

**What I changed**

- `backend/internal/repo/merchant.go` — added the missing `&p.ContentType` destination.
- `backend/internal/httpx/e2e_merchant_test.go` — new `TestMerchantCatalogRequestFlow`: seller lists (the regression), proposes, sees it pending with its content type, admin approves, the product appears in the catalogue with `contentType: dlc`. Passes against the Neon test branch.
- `backend/internal/db/seed.go` — `EnsureDemoRequest`: gives the demo seller one approved request on a fresh database, idempotent (inserts only when that seller has neither an approved request nor one for the same title), wired into the boot seed.
- `MerchantRequests.tsx` — an approved request now links to its catalogue listing instead of just saying "live in the catalog".

**On your second point:** production's demo seller already had **two** approved requests — "Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree" and "Grand Theft Auto VI" — you just couldn't see them because the list 500'd. Verified live after deploy: the page renders both with their DLC/FULL GAME badges, admin notes and the new links, and no error text. A fresh install now gets one approved request automatically.

**Verification:** the integration test passes against real Postgres; live `GET /api/merchant/requests` returns 200 with data; the production seller page renders cleanly. Gates: `go vet`, `go test ./...`, `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, lint 0 errors. Shipped as `b7dc9cd` (Render redeployed the API, Vercel the SPA).

One thing I deliberately did not do: production has no *pending* request, and I didn't want to leave junk in the queue — creation itself is covered by the integration test and returned 201 when I exercised it locally. If you'd like a pending row for the demo, submit one from the portal and I'll leave it for the admin queue to show.

// CreateRequest submits a new catalog title for admin approval.
func (m *Merchant) CreateRequest(ctx context.Context, merchantID int64, title, description, coverURL, platformSlug, regionCode, contentType string) (models.ProductRequest, error) {
	var id int64
	err := m.pool.QueryRow(ctx, `
		INSERT INTO product_requests (merchant_id, title, description, cover_url, platform_id, region_id, content_type)
		SELECT $1, $2, $3, $4, pl.id, r.id, $7
		FROM platforms pl, regions r
		WHERE pl.slug = $5 AND r.code = $6
		RETURNING id`,
		merchantID, title, description, coverURL, platformSlug, regionCode, contentType,
	).Scan(&id)
	if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
		return models.ProductRequest{}, ErrInvalidReference
	}
	if err != nil {
		return models.ProductRequest{}, fmt.Errorf("create product request: %w", err)
	}

	return m.RequestByID(ctx, id)
}

// RequestByID loads one request with its joined names.
func (m *Merchant) RequestByID(ctx context.Context, id int64) (models.ProductRequest, error) {
	var p models.ProductRequest
	err := m.pool.QueryRow(ctx, `
		SELECT pr.id, pr.merchant_id, u.display_name, pr.title,
		       pl.slug, r.code, pr.cover_url, pr.description, pr.content_type, pr.status, pr.admin_note,
		       p.slug, pr.created_at, pr.reviewed_at
		FROM product_requests pr
		JOIN users u      ON u.id = pr.merchant_id
		JOIN platforms pl ON pl.id = pr.platform_id
		JOIN regions r    ON r.id = pr.region_id
		LEFT JOIN products p ON p.id = pr.product_id
		WHERE pr.id = $1`, id,
	).Scan(&p.ID, &p.MerchantID, &p.MerchantName, &p.Title, &p.PlatformSlug, &p.RegionCode,
		&p.CoverURL, &p.Description, &p.ContentType, &p.Status, &p.AdminNote, &p.ProductSlug, &p.CreatedAt, &p.ReviewedAt)
	if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
		return p, ErrNotFound
	}
	return p, err
}

// Requests lists the merchant's catalog proposals.
func (m *Merchant) Requests(ctx context.Context, merchantID int64) ([]models.ProductRequest, error) {
	rows, err := m.pool.Query(ctx, `
		SELECT pr.id, pr.merchant_id, u.display_name, pr.title,
		       pl.slug, r.code, pr.cover_url, pr.description, pr.content_type, pr.status, pr.admin_note,
		       p.slug, pr.created_at, pr.reviewed_at
		FROM product_requests pr
		JOIN users u      ON u.id = pr.merchant_id
		JOIN platforms pl ON pl.id = pr.platform_id
		JOIN regions r    ON r.id = pr.region_id
		LEFT JOIN products p ON p.id = pr.product_id

// Seed populates an empty database. It is a no-op when products already exist,
// which keeps boot-time seeding idempotent across restarts and deploys.
func Seed(ctx context.Context, pool *pgxpool.Pool, games []seed.Game, secret []byte) error {
	var existing int
	if err := pool.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT count(*) FROM products`).Scan(&existing); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("count products: %w", err)
	}
	if existing > 0 {
		return nil
	}

	tx, err := pool.Begin(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback(ctx) }()

	platformIDs, err := insertLookup(ctx, tx, "platforms", "slug", "name",
		func(i int) (string, string) { return seedPlatforms[i].Slug, seedPlatforms[i].Name }, len(seedPlatforms), func(i int) int16 { return seedPlatforms[i].Sort })
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	regionIDs, err := insertLookup(ctx, tx, "regions", "code", "name",
		func(i int) (string, string) { return seedRegions[i].Code, seedRegions[i].Name }, len(seedRegions), func(i int) int16 { return seedRegions[i].Sort })
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	genreIDs, err := insertLookup(ctx, tx, "genres", "slug", "name",
		func(i int) (string, string) { return seedGenres[i].Slug, seedGenres[i].Name }, len(seedGenres), nil)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	// --- accounts ----------------------------------------------------------
	if _, err := insertUser(ctx, tx, AdminEmail, AdminPassword, "Keyforge Admin", "admin", true); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if _, err := insertUser(ctx, tx, CustomerEmail, CustomerPass, "Demo Buyer", "customer", true); err != nil {

func (m *Merchant) Requests(ctx context.Context, merchantID int64) ([]models.ProductRequest, error) {
	rows, err := m.pool.Query(ctx, `
		SELECT pr.id, pr.merchant_id, u.display_name, pr.title,
		       pl.slug, r.code, pr.cover_url, pr.description, pr.content_type, pr.status, pr.admin_note,
		       p.slug, pr.created_at, pr.reviewed_at
		FROM product_requests pr
		JOIN users u      ON u.id = pr.merchant_id
		JOIN platforms pl ON pl.id = pr.platform_id
		JOIN regions r    ON r.id = pr.region_id
		LEFT JOIN products p ON p.id = pr.product_id
		WHERE pr.merchant_id = $1
		ORDER BY pr.created_at DESC`, merchantID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("list product requests: %w", err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()

	out := []models.ProductRequest{}
	for rows.Next() {
		var p models.ProductRequest
		if err := rows.Scan(&p.ID, &p.MerchantID, &p.MerchantName, &p.Title,
			&p.PlatformSlug, &p.RegionCode, &p.CoverURL, &p.Description, &p.Status,
			&p.AdminNote, &p.ProductSlug, &p.CreatedAt, &p.ReviewedAt); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		out = append(out, p)
	}
	return out, rows.Err()
}

// demoRequestProduct is the catalogue title the demo seller's reviewed request
// points at: one with offers, so the merchant can go straight to listing it.
const demoRequestProduct = "elden-ring"

// EnsureDemoRequest gives the first demo seller one already-reviewed catalogue
// request. Without it a reviewer opening the merchant portal sees an empty list
// and cannot tell the approve flow ever works.
//
// It is idempotent and safe on every boot: it inserts only when that seller has
// neither an approved request nor one for the same title, so restarts and
// redeploys add nothing.
func EnsureDemoRequest(ctx context.Context, pool *pgxpool.Pool) error {
	_, err := pool.Exec(ctx, `
		INSERT INTO product_requests (
			merchant_id, title, description, cover_url, platform_id, region_id,
			content_type, status, admin_note, reviewed_by, reviewed_at, product_id)
		SELECT seller.id, p.title, p.description, p.cover_url, pl.id, r.id,
		       p.content_type, 'approved',
		       'Approved — the title is in the catalogue, list your keys against it.',
		       admin.id, now(), p.id
		FROM users seller
		JOIN users admin    ON admin.email = $1
		JOIN products p     ON p.slug = $3
		JOIN platforms pl   ON pl.slug = 'steam'
		JOIN regions r      ON r.code = 'GLOBAL'
		WHERE seller.email = $2
		  AND NOT EXISTS (
		        SELECT 1 FROM product_requests pr
		        WHERE pr.merchant_id = seller.id
		          AND (pr.status = 'approved' OR pr.title = p.title))`,
		AdminEmail, fmt.Sprintf(demoMerchantAt, 1), demoRequestProduct)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("ensure demo request: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}
GOEOF

{
  "message": "Found and fixed the real cause, and it is worse than the page suggests: **the merchant's whole request list was returning HTTP 500 in every environment**, not just on submit.\n\n- `Merchant.Requests` selects 14 columns but scanned into 13 destinations — the `content_type` column was added to the query and never to the scan. Postgres rejects the row shape, so `GET /api/merchant/requests` answered `internal_error` → the page fell back to \"something went wrong\".\n- Submitting worked all along (201 locally); it was loading the list that failed. That is why the seller saw the generic error on the page.\n- Fix: added `&p.ContentType` in the right position (`backend/internal/repo/merchant.go`).\n\nI also added the missing regression test — `TestMerchantCatalogRequestFlow` walks the whole lifecycle (seller lists, proposes, sees it pending, admin approves, product appears with its content type) — and it passes against the Neon test branch.\n\nOn your second point: production's demo seller already had **two** approved requests (\"Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree\", \"Grand Theft Auto VI\"); they were invisible only because the list 500'd. For a fresh database I added an idempotent `EnsureDemoRequest` fixture, so a new install gets one approved request automatically, and approved rows now link to their catalogue listing.\n\nNext: commit, ship, verify the endpoint answers 200 on production.",
  "title": "Seller request list 500'd everywhere: 14 columns, 13 scan targets"
}

## Turn 33

### User

where is the tabs in row menu in merchant/admin portal - add styling so it would be more clear that it's a menu rathar than just tranperant bg

### Assistant

Both portals share the same stripped-down tag list — plain text on transparent purple. I'll extract one styled tab strip and use it in both.

On a phone the active tab sits off-screen. Making the strip scroll the current section into view.

The section menu lives in the portal shells — `features/merchant/MerchantLayout.tsx` and `features/admin/AdminLayout.tsx`, just under the portal title. Both were rendering the links as loose text straight on the purple band, which is exactly why it read as a sentence rather than navigation.

**What it looks like now**

A single bordered, filled tab strip: a dark panel (`bg-brand-800/60`, `border-white/15`, 1 px inset highlight, `backdrop-blur`) holding the sections, with the current one as a solid yellow tab and the others sitting flat on the bar with a hover state. Both shells share one new component, `components/SectionTabs.tsx`, so the merchant portal's three tabs and the back-office's eight can't drift apart.

One extra thing the phone view exposed: with eight admin sections the strip scrolls sideways, but it used to start at the far left, leaving "Orders & ledger" off-screen even while you were on that page. The strip now centres the active tab on every navigation (without scrolling the page itself), so the current section is always visible.

**Verified** — 9/9 in headless Chrome, locally and again on production after deploy: merchant strip has all 3 sections with the active tab filled yellow (`rgb(250, 211, 24)` on `rgb(20, 16, 31)`), admin strip has all 8 and marks "ORDERS & LEDGER", the phone version scrolls (`scrolls=true`) with the active tab in view and no page-level horizontal overflow.

Shipped as `41c63a6`, deployed to Vercel. Gates clean: `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, lint 0 errors.

## Turn 34

### User

add ability to choose currency and region at the top near the cart, depending on chosen region select automatically products matching users region, if no available default to global, if available check if global keys or regional keys are cheaper and select by that

### Assistant

Good scope. Let me look at how the catalogue aggregates offers today, since the region rule has to apply in four places (store, search, homepage rows, related).

Now the search query and the handlers.

Markets work server-side (TR cheaper on 13 of 60 titles, others fall back to GLOBAL). Now the frontend.

Now the header control and the four consumers.

Now the store hint, then a full build and browser check.

Core behaviour is right (TR 34.99 vs EU 44.99) — my request capture was attached to the wrong CDP socket. Fixing the harness.

Shipped as `6faf5e7` and verified on production.

**The control:** a market menu sits next to the cart where the old bare "EU · EUR" text was. One button (`🇪🇺 EU · EUR ▾`) opens a panel with **Keys you can activate** (Europe, United States, UK, Turkey, Brazil, Global keys only) and **Show prices in** (EUR / USD / GBP). The choice is remembered in `localStorage`, and changing it reloads the catalogue so nothing keeps an old price.

**How the region decides what you see**

- Every catalogue request now carries `market=REGION`. The price aggregate only counts offers from that region or `GLOBAL` ones, and because it takes `MIN()`, **you always see the cheaper of the two** — that is the rule you asked for, implemented once in the shared offer CTE so the store, homepage rows, search and the "you might also like" row can't disagree.
- **Fallback to global is automatic**: most titles have global keys, so a market with no regional sellers still shows the full catalogue at global prices — no retry, no empty page.
- **Explicit region chips win**: tick "US" in the store filters and the market preference is dropped for that view, with a line in the filter panel saying so; with no chips ticked it reads "Following your market: TR. Every price is the cheaper of a TR key and a global one."

**Evidence**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Same game, different markets (Red Dead Redemption 2) | EU **€44.99**, TR **€34.99**, BR €44.99, GLOBAL €44.99 — regional key wins when cheaper |
| Never above global | 4/4 sampled titles: TR ≤ min(EU, GLOBAL) |
| Market with no regional sellers | `market=GLOBAL` still lists all 81 products |
| Requests carry the market | store `market=TR` ✓, homepage ✓, search ✓, related ✓ |
| Region chip override | `?region=US` sends `region=US` and **no** `market=` |
| Currency inside the panel | 50 `€` → 0 `€` and 50 `US$` after switching to USD, live |
| Gates | `go vet`, `go test ./...`, `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, lint 0 errors |

Two notes for the review: the market is *pricing*, not *entitlement* — the product page still lists every seller's offer with its region chip so a buyer can compare, and checkout charges what the cart was priced at. And the currency remains a fixed-rate display (a 1.08 demo rate), stated in the panel itself, because the backend stores and charges euro cents only.

type CatalogFilter struct {
	Search        string
	Platforms     []string
	Regions       []string
	Genres        []string
	ContentTypes  []string
	MinPriceCents *int
	MaxPriceCents *int
	Sort          string
	Page          int
	PageSize      int
	// IncludeUnlisted keeps products that have no live offers yet. The storefront
	// never wants those, but a merchant listing a freshly approved catalogue entry
	// does: that product exists before any offer points at it.
	IncludeUnlisted bool

// titleAcronymExpr builds a product title's initialism in SQL — "Grand Theft
// Auto V" becomes "gtav" — so a shopper typing "gta", "bg3" or "rdr2" finds the
// game. Trigram similarity cannot reach those: they share almost no characters
// with the full title. Comparing by prefix keeps it cheap and predictable.
const titleAcronymExpr = `(SELECT string_agg(left(w, 1), '' ORDER BY ord)
					FROM regexp_split_to_table(regexp_replace(lower(p.title), '''', '', 'g'), '[^a-z0-9]+')
					     WITH ORDINALITY AS t(w, ord)
					WHERE w <> '')`

// sortClauses is a whitelist: the client picks a key, never SQL. This avoids
// injection while still supporting the store's sort options.
var sortClauses = map[string]string{
	"relevance":  "score DESC, p.popularity DESC, p.title ASC",
	"popular":    "p.popularity DESC, p.title ASC",
	"price_asc":  "min_price ASC, p.title ASC",
	"price_desc": "min_price DESC, p.title ASC",
	"newest":     "p.release_date DESC NULLS LAST, p.title ASC",
	"discount":   "best_discount DESC, p.popularity DESC",
	"title":      "lower(p.title) ASC, p.title ASC",
}

const offerAggCTE = `
	offer_agg AS (
		SELECT o.product_id,
		       MIN(o.price_cents) AS min_price,
		       MAX(o.price_cents) AS max_price,
		       COUNT(*)::int      AS offer_count,
		       COALESCE(MAX(
		           CASE WHEN o.base_price_cents IS NOT NULL AND o.base_price_cents > o.price_cents
		                THEN ROUND((1 - o.price_cents::numeric / o.base_price_cents) * 100)
		                ELSE 0 END), 0)::int AS best_discount,
		       ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT pl.slug ORDER BY pl.slug) AS platform_slugs,
		       ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT r.code ORDER BY r.code)   AS region_codes
		FROM offers o
		JOIN platforms pl ON pl.id = o.platform_id
		JOIN regions   r  ON r.id  = o.region_id
		WHERE o.is_active
		  AND o.stock > 0
		  -- Platform/region filters narrow which offers contribute to the
		  -- displayed price, so a "PlayStation" filter never shows a Steam price.
		  AND (cardinality(@platforms::text[]) = 0 OR pl.slug = ANY(@platforms::text[]))
		  AND (cardinality(@regions::text[])   = 0 OR r.code  = ANY(@regions::text[]))
		GROUP BY o.product_id
	)`

func (c *Catalog) CardsByIDs(ctx context.Context, ids []int64) ([]models.ProductCard, error) {
	out := []models.ProductCard{}
	if len(ids) == 0 {
		return out, nil
	}
	rows, err := c.pool.Query(ctx, `
		WITH `+offerAggCTE+`
		SELECT p.id, p.slug, p.title, p.cover_url, p.release_date, p.popularity, p.content_type,
		       a.min_price, a.max_price, a.offer_count, a.best_discount,
		       a.platform_slugs, a.region_codes
		FROM products p
		JOIN offer_agg a ON a.product_id = p.id
		WHERE p.is_active AND p.id = ANY(@ids)
		ORDER BY array_position(@ids::bigint[], p.id)`,
		pgx.NamedArgs{"ids": ids, "platforms": []string{}, "regions": []string{}})
```

func marketParam(r *http.Request) string {
	code := strings.ToUpper(strings.TrimSpace(r.URL.Query().Get("market")))
	switch code {
	case "EU", "US", "UK", "TR", "BR":
		return code

func NewHomepage(pool *pgxpool.Pool) *Homepage { return &Homepage{pool: pool} }

// Blocks returns every visible block, each with its curated product list.
func (h *Homepage) Blocks(ctx context.Context) ([]models.HomepageBlock, error) {
	rows, err := h.pool.Query(ctx, `
		SELECT id, block_key, type, title, subtitle, config, position
		FROM homepage_blocks
		WHERE is_visible
		ORDER BY position ASC, id ASC`)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("list homepage blocks: %w", err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()

	var blocks []models.HomepageBlock
	ids := make([]int64, 0, 8)
	byID := make(map[int64]int, 8)

	for rows.Next() {
		var b models.HomepageBlock
		var raw []byte
		var position int
		if err := rows.Scan(&b.ID, &b.Key, &b.Type, &b.Title, &b.Subtitle, &raw, &position); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("scan block: %w", err)
		}
		if len(raw) > 0 {
			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &b.Config); err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode block config: %w", err)
			}
		}
		if b.Config == nil {
			b.Config = map[string]any{}
		}
		b.Products = []models.ProductCard{}
		byID[b.ID] = len(blocks)
		ids = append(ids, b.ID)
		blocks = append(blocks, b)
	}
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
			&card.Platforms, &card.Regions,
		); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("scan block product: %w", err)
		}
		idx, ok := byID[blockID]
		if !ok {
			continue
		}

	if err := prodRows.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, err

	// A block can follow the release calendar instead of a curated list, so the
	// homepage row refreshes itself as games come out.
	var auto []models.ProductCard
	for _, block := range blocks {
		if source, _ := block.Config["source"].(string); source == "new_releases" {
			if auto == nil {
				if auto, err = h.newReleases(ctx, 12); err != nil {
					return nil, err
				}

					blocks[i].Products = auto

			}
		}
	}
	return blocks, nil
}

// newReleases is the auto-updating source for a "new releases" row: games that are
// not out yet come first (soonest release first), then the most recently released
// titles, newest first. No arbitrary cut-off window — a quiet catalogue would
// otherwise render an empty row. Because it reads release_date on every request, a
// title stops being a pre-order the day it ships.
func (h *Homepage) newReleases(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]models.ProductCard, error) {
	rows, err := h.pool.Query(ctx, `
		SELECT p.id, p.slug, p.title, p.cover_url, p.release_date, p.popularity, p.content_type,
		       MIN(o.price_cents)::int AS min_price,
		       MAX(o.price_cents)::int AS max_price,
		       COUNT(o.id)::int        AS offer_count,
		       COALESCE(MAX(
		           CASE WHEN o.base_price_cents IS NOT NULL AND o.base_price_cents > o.price_cents
		                THEN ROUND((1 - o.price_cents::numeric / o.base_price_cents) * 100)
		                ELSE 0 END), 0)::int AS best_discount,
		       ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT pl.slug ORDER BY pl.slug) AS platform_slugs,
		       ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT r.code ORDER BY r.code)   AS region_codes
```

function AccountMenu() {
  const { user, signOut } = useAuth()
  const location = useLocation()
  const navigate = useNavigate()
  // Open state is keyed to the current location, so any navigation closes the
  // menu without an effect that would re-render on route changes.
  const locationKey = `${location.pathname}${location.search}`
  const [openKey, setOpenKey] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const open = openKey === locationKey
  const close = () => setOpenKey(null)
  const containerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)

  // Close on outside click or Escape — a <details> element does neither, which is
  // why this is a controlled popover.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!open) return
    function onPointerDown(event: MouseEvent) {
      if (!containerRef.current?.contains(event.target as Node)) setOpenKey(null)
    }
    function onKeyDown(event: KeyboardEvent) {
      if (event.key === 'Escape') setOpenKey(null)
    }
    document.addEventListener('mousedown', onPointerDown)
    document.addEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown)
    return () => {
      document.removeEventListener('mousedown', onPointerDown)
      document.removeEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown)
    }
  }, [open])

{
  "content": "import { createContext, useContext, useEffect, useMemo, useState } from 'react'\nimport type { ReactNode } from 'react'\n\nimport { CURRENCIES, setActiveCurrency } from '@/lib/currency'\nimport type { CurrencyCode } from '@/lib/currency'\n\n/**\n * The visitor's market: which region's keys they can activate, and how prices are\n * printed. It is a preference, not a filter — every catalogue request carries it,\n * and the API prices a card from the visitor's region or a global key, whichever\n * is cheaper, falling back to global when the region has nothing to sell.\n */\nexport const REGIONS = [\n  { code: 'EU', label: 'Europe', flag: '🇪🇺' },\n  { code: 'US', label: 'United States', flag: '🇺🇸' },\n  { code: 'UK', label: 'United Kingdom', flag: '🇬🇧' },\n  { code: 'TR', label: 'Turkey', flag: '🇹🇷' },\n  { code: 'BR', label: 'Brazil', flag: '🇧🇷' },\n  { code: 'GLOBAL', label: 'Global keys only', flag: '🌍' },\n] as const\n\nexport type RegionCode = (typeof REGIONS)[number]['code']\n\ntype MarketState = {\n  currency: CurrencyCode\n  setCurrency: (code: CurrencyCode) => void\n  region: RegionCode\n  setRegion: (code: RegionCode) => void\n}\n\nconst REGION_KEY = 'keyforge.region'\nconst CURRENCY_KEY = 'keyforge.currency'\n\nconst MarketContext = createContext<MarketState | null>(null)\n\nfunction readStored<T extends string>(key: string, allowed: readonly string[], fallback: T): T {\n  try {\n    const stored = localStorage.getItem(key)\n    if (stored && allowed.includes(stored)) return stored as T\n  } catch {\n    // Private mode: fall back to the default market.\n  }\n  return fallback\n}\n\n/**\n * Holds market state. `formatMoney` and the catalogue client read module-level\n * values, so the provider writes them before children render — hence the\n * assignment during render rather than in an effect, which would flash the\n * previous currency. Changing either value remounts the tree beneath it, which is\n * how every price and every request picks up the new market at once.\n */\nexport function MarketProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  const [currency, setCurrencyState] = useState<CurrencyCode>(\n    () => readStored(CURRENCY_KEY, CURRENCIES, 'EUR'),\n  )\n  const [region, setRegionState] = useState<RegionCode>(\n    () => readStored(REGION_KEY, REGIONS.map((entry) => entry.code), 'EU'),\n  )\n  setActiveCurrency(currency)\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    try {\n      localStorage.setItem(CURRENCY_KEY, currency)\n      localStorage.setItem(REGION_KEY, region)\n    } catch {\n      // Remembering the choice is a nicety, not a requirement.\n    }\n  }, [currency, region])\n\n  const value = useMemo<MarketState>(\n    () => ({\n      currency,\n      setCurrency: setCurrencyState,\n      region,\n      setRegion: setRegionState,\n    }),\n    [currency, region],\n  )\n\n  return (\n    <MarketContext.Provider value={value}>\n      <div key={`${currency}-${region}`} className=\"contents\">\n        {children}\n      </div>\n    </MarketContext.Provider>\n  )\n}\n\nexport function useMarket() {\n  const ctx = useContext(MarketContext)\n  if (!ctx) throw new Error('useMarket must be used inside MarketProvider')\n  return ctx\n}\n",

#### Tool Call: Bash (`cd /c/Users/Minda/Downloads/kimi/homework2026 && grep -n "api/products?market" docs/api.md | head -2; cat >> docs/api.md <<'EOF'

### Market region

`market=EU|US|UK|TR|BR|GLOBAL` is the visitor's own region, not a filter. Cards are priced
from offers in that region or global ones only, and because the price aggregate takes
`MIN()`, the buyer always sees the cheaper of the two. A product with neither a regional
nor a global offer is not listed — which is also why a market with no regional sellers
still shows the catalogue: global keys carry it. `market` appears on `/api/products`,
`/api/search`, `/api/homepage` and `/api/products/{slug}` (for the "you might also like"
row). An explicit `region=` filter on the store wins over it, and an unknown value is
treated as "no preference" rather than an error.
EOF
git add -A backend frontend/src docs PROGRESS.md && git commit -q -m "feat(market): pick a region and currency in the header, price by it

- header gains a market menu next to the cart: region + display currency
- catalogue, search, homepage rows and related products take market=REGION and
  price from that region or GLOBAL keys, whichever is cheaper
- a market with no regional sellers still lists the catalogue through global keys
- an explicit region chip on the store overrides the market
- price aggregates move into the shared offer CTE, so all four surfaces agree" 2>&1 | tail -1; git log --oneline -1`)

### Assistant

A mobile pass, then. First I'll measure every route at 390 px and find what actually overflows instead of guessing.

No page-level overflow, but two real problems: the header clips its right-hand items and the market panel opens off-screen. Measuring the header at 390 and 360.

Now the header fix: compact controls on phones, and a viewport-anchored market sheet.

Zero overflow across 46 checks now. Let me look at how the pages actually feel on a phone.

Fixed and live as `01f9985`. I measured every route on a phone rather than guessing at the two you named.

**What was actually wrong**

- **Register button:** at 360 px the row ended at 359 px of 360 — one pixel of slack, so on a real device with different font metrics it clipped. Fixed by shrinking the logo on phones (`1.15rem`), turning "Log in" into a person icon with an `aria-label`, a compact Register button, and tighter gaps. It now ends at **309/320px, 344/360 and 374/390** — 11–16 px of margin at every width.
- **Region menu:** `right-0` was anchored to a 50 px button sitting mid-row, so the 288 px panel grew leftwards and opened at **left: −113 px**, off-screen. On phones it is now a bottom sheet (`fixed inset-x-0 bottom-0`, max 75 vh, scrollable); it measures **left 0, right 390, top 450, bottom 844** — fully on screen. Desktop keeps the dropdown.

**Sweep across all pages** — 46 checks at 320 and 390 px over guest, customer, merchant and admin routes: **0 overflow**. The clunky parts I found and fixed:

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| Back-office / merchant tables | They needed 720–900 px and showed two columns on a phone. Least important columns (Items, Created, Orders, Spent, Joined, Keys sold, Status) hide below 640 px, min-widths drop to 420–520, and a new `TableShell` adds a right-edge fade plus "Swipe the table sideways for the remaining columns" |
| Stat tiles | Two-up on phones instead of full-width stacks, so the ledger fits in one screen |
| Order rows | Reference no longer wraps mid-code; buyer e-mail truncates |
| Spacing | `PageBand` and the home page drop `py-8/16` to `py-5/8` on phones, the store's `py-8` becomes `py-4`, and the hero block goes from `min-h-360px` to `240` — roughly 250 px of dead space removed before the first product |
| Market picker, store filters | Store hint now says the market is followed; filter panel unchanged but opens compactly |

**Verification:** local audit 46/46 with no overflow, re-run against production after deploy — same 46/46, the sheet fits, and the header rows measured at 320/360/390 with no clipped element. `tsc`, `npm run build`, `go vet`, `go test ./...` all green, lint 0 errors.

One judgement call worth knowing: I hid table columns rather than converting the back-office tables into cards. It keeps one markup path per table and keeps the numbers side by side, at the cost of a swipe on small screens — which the fade and hint now make explicit.

The table keeps its columns (a back-office needs them),\n * so the shell says so: the container scrolls sideways, a fade on the right edge\n * shows there is more, and a line of text spells it out for anyone who does not\n * think to swipe. Above `sm` the hint disappears — a laptop needs no coach.\n */\nexport function TableShell({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  return (\n    <div>\n      <div className=\"relative\">\n        <div className=\"overflow-x-auto\">{children}</div>\n        <div\n          aria-hidden\n          className=\"pointer-events-none absolute inset-y-0 right-0 w-8 bg-gradient-to-l from-canvas to-transparent sm:hidden\"\n        />\n      </div>\n      <p className=\"px-4 py-2 text-xs text-brand-300 sm:hidden\">\n        Swipe the table sideways for the remaining columns.\n      </p>\n    </div>\n  )\n}\n",

## Turn 36

### User

check desptop and mobile if everything is looking good and no visual bugs on both of them

### Assistant

A final visual QA pass, then. I'll audit every route at desktop and phone widths for overflow, broken images, console errors and clipped controls.

Two real bugs: the catalogue editor renders `<img src="">` for a product without cover art (broken image + React warning), and the market button is under a comfortable tap height.

Two polish items from the screenshots: the scrolled tab strip shows a clipped label, and the desktop buy box is too wide.

Checked both sizes across the whole site — 22 routes × 2 viewports = 44 page loads, locally and again against production after deploy.

**Automated sweep: clean**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Horizontal overflow (1440 and 390) | **0** |
| Broken images | **0** |
| Console errors / runtime exceptions | **0** |
| Collapsed or empty panels | 0 real (4 flags were the ticket and request textareas — my detector matching the element itself) |
| Tap targets under 32 px on phones | only inline nav links inside the 44 px nav strip — left as is |

**What the sweep and screenshots caught, now fixed and live in `9a51213`**

- **Admin catalogue drew a broken image** — a product without artwork rendered `<img src="">`, which the browser reads as "the current page" (it also logged a React warning). All back-office and merchant thumbnails now use a `CoverThumb` that shows a placeholder box.
- **Market button** was 30 px tall on a phone; now 40 px.
- **Portal section strip** cut a label at the screen edge when scrolled; it now fades at both edges so a half-label reads as "more this way".
- **Desktop buy box** stretched ~660 px wide; capped at `max-w-xl` so the price, CTA and Compare button stay a unit.

**Things I looked at and judged fine:** home (hero, platform strip, rows), store (filters button, sort, 2-up grid), product page (facts strip, price block, anchors, clamped description), cart, checkout (payment cards, summary with Edit cart and tax line), sign-in/up, orders, wallet, support, receipt, merchant overview/offers/requests, and all eight admin tabs.

**One honest caveat:** the header has 11–16 px of slack at 320–390 px. That is comfortable for the widths I measured, but a device with unusually large system text could still squeeze it; the structural fix would be moving Sign in/Register into the second nav row, which I did not do because it changes the header's information hierarchy.

Repo is clean apart from your three session exports, local servers are stopped, and the last three commits are the mobile fix, the visual fix, and the QA notes in `PROGRESS.md`.

/**
 * Thumbnail for back-office lists. Same idea as `Cover`, but a product without
 * artwork gets a placeholder box instead of an empty `src` — an empty string is
 * not "no image" to a browser, it means "the current page".
 */
export function CoverThumb({
  productId,
  url,
  className = '',
  label = 'No cover',
}: {
  productId?: number
  url?: string
  className?: string
  label?: string
}) {
  if (!url) {
    return (
      <div className={`grid place-items-center bg-canvas text-center text-[0.6rem] leading-tight text-ink-300 ${className}`}>
        {label}
      </div>
    )
  }
  return (
    <Cover
      productId={productId}
      url={url}
      alt=""
      sizes="80px"
      widths={[160, 240]}
      fallbackWidth={160}
      loading="lazy"
      className={className}
    />
  )
}
EOF

exceptions** at either size; the remaining flags are inline nav links inside the 44 px

Bugs it caught and closed:

  \`content_type\` into 13 scan destinations, so Postgres rejected every row and the portal

  to 320 px.

  now, fully inside the viewport.
- **Wide tables** (720–900 px) got \`TableShell\`: least-important columns hide below 640 px,

  space before the first product on a phone.
- Portal section strip fades at both edges while scrolled; a phone also scrolls the active
  tab into view.

`

## Turn 37

### User

in admin homepage panel, there is list of 10 items per panel, but it only shows 5 and on mobile best would be 6

### Assistant

Found it: the homepage carousel renders `block.products.slice(0, 5)` regardless of how many products the block holds. Fixing that, with a 6-card cap below `sm` as you suggested.

Desktop now shows all 10, but `new_releases` has 12 and leaves two orphans in a 5-column row. I'll cap the row at two tidy rows.

Fixed and live in `d48eea6`.

**Cause:** the homepage carousel hardcoded `block.products.slice(0, 5)` in `features/home/blocks.tsx` — the grid has five columns, so five cards looked like intent, but the block data was ignored past the fifth. The admin Homepage panel's live preview renders through that same component, so it inherited the cap: 10 products in the editor, 5 on screen, which reads as data loss.

**Now:**
- Rows render **every product the editor curated**, capped at **two full rows (10)** on wide screens and **6 (three rows of two)** on a phone.
- The 10-item blocks show all 10; the auto `new_releases` row holds 12 and shows its first 10 rather than leaving two orphans alone on a third row.
- `ProductCard` gained an optional `className`, so the cap is a CSS breakpoint on the card itself — no wrapper divs, no change to card heights.

**Verified against production:**

| Row | Before | Desktop now | Phone now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best sellers | 5 | 10 | 6 |
| Flash deals | 5 | 10 | 6 |
| New releases | 5 | 10 (of 12) | 6 |
| Great games under €15 | 5 | 10 | 6 |

Measured by counting visible cards per section, locally and again on the live site after deploy; `tsc`, `npm run build` and lint are clean. The admin preview matches by construction, so what the editor shows is what the homepage renders.

function CarouselBlock({ block }: { block: HomeBlockData }) {
  if (block.products.length === 0) return null
  const href = str(block.config, 'href')
  const tone = str(block.config, 'tone')

  return (
    <section className="container-page mt-10">
      <div className="mb-5 flex flex-wrap items-end justify-between gap-3">
        <div>
          <h2 className="flex items-center gap-2 font-display text-2xl font-extrabold text-white sm:text-[1.75rem]">
            {block.title}
            {tone === 'accent' && (
              <span className="rounded-[2px] bg-accent-500 px-2 py-0.5 label-caps text-on-accent">Hot</span>
            )}
          </h2>
          {block.subtitle && <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-brand-100">{block.subtitle}</p>}
        </div>
        {href && (
          <Link
            to={href}
            className="shrink-0 rounded-[2px] border border-white/40 px-4 py-2 text-xs font-extrabold uppercase tracking-wide text-white transition hover:border-accent-500 hover:text-accent-500"
          >
            View all
          </Link>
        )}
      </div>

      <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-3 sm:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-5">
        {block.products.slice(0, 5).map((product) => (
          <ProductCard key={product.id} product={product} />
        ))}
      </div>
    </section>
  )
}

function BannerBlock({ block }: { block: HomeBlockData }) {
  const items = Array.isArray(block.config.items)
    ? (block.config.items as { title: string; text: string }[])
    : []

  return (
    <section className="container-page mt-12">
      <div className="bg-brand-900 p-6 text-white sm:p-8">
        <h2 className="font-display text-xl font-extrabold sm:text-2xl">{block.title}</h2>
        <div className="mt-5 grid gap-3 sm:grid-cols-3">
          {items.map((item) => (
            <div key={item.title} className="rounded-[2px] bg-brand-800 p-4">
              <p className="text-sm font-extrabold text-accent-500">{item.title}</p>
              <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-brand-200">{item.text}</p>
=== admin preview
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

/** Renders the block with the draft values, using the same component the homepage
 *  uses, so what you see here is what ships. */
function BlockPreview({ draft, config }: { draft: BlockDraft; config: Record<string, unknown> }) {
  const [cards, setCards] = useState<HomeBlockData['products']>([])
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const autoSourced = config.source === 'new_releases'
  const ids = draft.products.map((product) => product.id).join(',')

  useEffect(() => {
    if (autoSourced || ids === '') {
      setCards([])
      return
    }
    let cancelled = false
    setLoading(true)
    adminApi
      .blockCards(ids.split(',').map(Number))
      .then(({ cards: fetched }) => {
        if (cancelled) return
        setCards(fetched)
        setError(null)
      })
      .catch((err: unknown) => {
        if (cancelled) return
        setCards([])
        setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Could not build the preview')
      })
      .finally(() => {
        if (!cancelled) setLoading(false)
      })
    return () => {
      cancelled = true
    }
  }, [ids, autoSourced])

  const block: HomeBlockData = {
    key: draft.key,
    type: draft.type,
    title: draft.title,
    subtitle: draft.subtitle,
    config,
    products: cards,
  }

  return (
    <div className="rounded-[2px] border border-dashed border-white/30 p-3">
      <p className="mb-3 text-xs font-extrabold uppercase tracking-wide text-brand-200">
        Preview — {draft.isVisible ? 'visible on the homepage' : 'hidden, so it would not render'}
      </p>
      {autoSourced ? (
        <Notice tone="info">
          This block follows the release calendar (<code>source: new_releases</code>), so the live row is filled
          from products&apos; release dates rather than this list.
        </Notice>
      ) : error ? (
        <ErrorNote message={error} />
      ) : loading ? (
        <Skeleton className="h-40 w-full" />
      ) : draft.products.length === 0 && ['product_carousel', 'platform_strip', 'hero'].includes(draft.type) ? (
        <Notice tone="warning">Add at least one product to see this block rendered.</Notice>
